claims.text: Conventional steel rollers and guide plates are susceptible to corrosion by molten aluminum during hot-dip aluminum plating.
A high-alumina ceramic coating can be applied to steel components by thermal spraying or chemical vapor deposition.
The coated components would be exposed to high-temperature molten aluminum for extended operational periods.
The applied coating forms a durable high-alumina Al2O3 layer.
High-alumina Al2O3 is chemically inert toward molten aluminum under the proposed hot-dip conditions.
The alumina layer acts as a physical barrier between the steel substrate and molten aluminum.
Preventing direct contact between steel and molten aluminum inhibits chemical reactions responsible for corrosion and erosion.
A stable oxide layer formed on alumina contributes to high-temperature chemical inertness.
High-alumina-coated steel components will have a significantly lower corrosion and erosion rate than untreated steel under identical molten-aluminum process conditions.
High-alumina-coated steel components will have a longer service life than untreated steel components under identical process conditions.
Extreme changes in temperature or chemical reactivity may alter the protective effectiveness of the alumina coating.
The long-term adhesion strength of the alumina coating under thermal cycling and mechanical stress has not been fully quantified.
The optimal alumina-coating thickness and deposition parameters for maximum protection have not been established.
